source_rationale: PECAM1 (CD31) and CDH5 (VE-cadherin) are pan-endothelial markers essential for cell-cell adhesion and vascular integrity, present across all endothelial subtypes. MECOM and ENPEP further confirm endothelial identity. BTNL9, RBP7, and CA4 are enriched in capillary endothelial cells specifically, with CA4 (carbonic anhydrase 4) being a well-established capillary EC marker in adipose tissue. Together these markers identify capillary ECs and distinguish them from arterial, venous, and lymphatic endothelial subtypes.

source_rationale: PECAM1 (CD31) and CDH5 (VE-cadherin) are pan-endothelial markers confirming endothelial identity, while MECOM and ENPEP further support this. PROX1 is a transcription factor required for lymphatic endothelial cell specification and maintenance, and LYVE1 (lymphatic vessel endothelial hyaluronan receptor 1) is expressed on the surface of lymphatic endothelial cells and involved in hyaluronan uptake. Together these markers identify lymphatic ECs and distinguish them from capillary, arterial, and venous endothelial subtypes.

source_rationale: MYOCD (myocardin) is a transcription factor driving smooth muscle cell differentiation and is enriched in smooth muscle cells. MYH11 (smooth muscle myosin heavy chain) is a contractile protein with enriched expression in mature smooth muscle cells. Together these markers reliably identify smooth muscle cells within the mural cell compartment and distinguish them from pericytes and other stromal populations.
_cap_dataset_name: Human Adipose Tissue Atlas v1.0 — Vascular cells

source_rationale: STEAP4 (STEAP family member 4) and COL25A1 (collagen type XXV alpha 1) show enriched expression in pericytes in single-nucleus adipose tissue datasets, and are used here to identify this population. Together these markers identify pericytes within the mural cell compartment and distinguish them from smooth muscle cells and stromal populations in adipose tissue.
